title: Performance panel deep dives
purpose: Go deeper into long tasks and yielding, and into the Core Web Vitals that the live metrics view and trace tracks show.
summary: A short deck on where page time goes. The main path covers the working loop, the long-task rule, the live metrics view and when to use each. One deep dive explains why the main thread blocks input and how scheduler.yield() splits work. The other shows how INP and CLS appear in a trace: the Interactions track, the Layout shifts track and the Insights tab.
explanation: Live metrics tell you that something is slow; a trace tells you which task made it slow and why input had to wait.

learning_check.question: What is the blocking period of a 90 ms task?
learning_check.answer: 40 ms: the task time minus 50 ms.

slides.heading: Where did the time go?
slides.notes: Ask the learner how they would find out why one click on a page feels slow.

slides.heading: The working loop
slides.notes: Reveal one step at a time. Live metrics come first, a trace only when the problem repeats.

items: Read live metrics: LCP, CLS, INP
Record a trace when it repeats
Find red marks in the Main track
Use Bottom-up to find the function

slides.heading: The 50 ms rule
slides.notes: A task over 50 ms gets a red triangle, and only the time past 50 ms is shaded red.

visual.verdict: Only the time past 50 ms is red.

slides.heading: Live metrics first
slides.notes: The live metrics screen updates as you use the page, including soft navigations in single-page apps.

items: LCP, CLS and INP update as you use the page
A SOFT NAV badge marks client-side navigations
Turn on field data to compare with real users

hotspots.label: Core Web Vitals in a trace

slides.heading: Metrics spot, traces explain
slides.notes: Live metrics are cheap and always on; a trace costs a recording but shows each task.

slides.heading: One task at a time
slides.notes: The main thread can only process one task at a time, so input that arrives during a long task must wait.

items: The main thread runs one task at a time
A click during a long task must wait
Blocking period: task time minus 50 ms

slides.heading: Split the work
slides.notes: Breaking a long task into smaller ones lets the browser respond to input between the pieces.

visual.verdict: Same work, input runs between pieces.

slides.heading: await scheduler.yield()
slides.notes: The await pauses the function; the browser can run input first, then the function continues where it left off.

items: Input can run before the rest
The function continues where it stopped
Not in all browsers: use a fallback

sequences.label: Core Web Vitals in a trace

slides.heading: INP: the Interactions track
slides.notes: Interactions over 200 ms get a red triangle; the tooltip splits the time into three parts.

slides.heading: CLS: the Layout shifts track
slides.notes: Each layout shift is a purple diamond; hover highlights the element, click shows the score and likely culprits.

items: Each shift is a purple diamond

slides.heading: The Insights tab
slides.notes: The Insights tab in the left sidebar groups findings such as LCP and INP subparts and third parties.

items: Open Insights in the left sidebar
